theme: 3 SwiftUI modifiers for paging and snapping scroll views

terms.definition: A modifier that adds space around the content of a scroll view.

video.description:
Learn to explain how to build paging and snapping scroll views in SwiftUI: contentMargins, scrollTargetBehavior & scrollTargetLayout, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
contentMargins - A modifier that adds space around the content of a scroll view.
scrollTargetBehavior - A modifier that tells a scroll view where to stop, such as one page at a time.
scrollTargetLayout - A modifier that marks the views inside a container as places where scrolling can stop.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain contentMargins, scrollTargetBehavior and scrollTargetLayout in English?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my photo carousel scrolls, but it never stops on a photo.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So scrollTargetBehavior tells the scroll view where to stop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. With `.paging`, it moves one page at a time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I added it, but it still does not snap.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Your photos are in a stack, so mark that stack with scrollTargetLayout.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh, so scrollTargetLayout shows which views are the targets?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Without it, the scroll view does not know where to snap.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now it works. But the first photo touches the edge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use contentMargins to add space around the content.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does contentMargins move the scroll bar too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Only if you choose the scroll bar area. Use `.scrollContent` for the content only.
Add contentMargins to give the scroll space.
